_comment: THE cross-language warnings-sink contract. Every agent-repl runtime writes
its warn and error records ONLY to a warnings file beside its log, and its
debug and info records only to the log itself, so a reader that wants
warnings and errors (bin/logs.sh --level warn, the deploy intake, the
harvest) opens the small warnings files alone instead of filtering every
record ever written (2026-11-17: 10 GB of logs outlived the intake's
their routing and naming against this file.
warnings_levels are the levels routed to the warnings file; every other
level goes to the log. A path's warnings file is named by inserting
'.warn' before a final '.log' extension, or appending '.warn.log' when the
path has none. A per-workspace sink named N (a canonical link N.log) has
its warnings twin named N.warn (a canonical link N.warn.log).
